content:
Tonight I’ll be speaking with Ben, who is from Georgia and was a neighbor of the older couple whose property was investigated by Sheriff’s Deputy James Patrick Akin after the couple made several 911 calls reporting a strange creature.

During his investigation, Jim would go on to cast a set of tracks that became known as the Elkins Creek Cast. Ben has his own experiences from living in the area, and tonight he’ll be sharing what he witnessed from his time there.

The Jim Akin and Elkins Creek Bigfoot story

The Elkins Creek Cast comes from a strange series of incidents in Pike County, Georgia, in 1994, involving retired Pike County sheriff’s deputy James Patrick Akin

The strange calls from an elderly couple

According to Akin’s account, an elderly couple lived on a rural property alongside Elkins Creek. They began repeatedly calling the Pike County Sheriff’s Office because something seemed to be visiting their property at night.

The reports became increasingly bizarre:

  • Something was tapping or banging on the outside of their home.
  • The couple reported something looking through their windows.
  • They heard strange noises and growling.
  • Their dogs began disappearing or were killed.
  • Dog food and corn were being taken.
  • A barn was damaged while something apparently tried to get at the food.
  • The couple eventually believed whatever was visiting them was deliberately interacting with them.

Akin was dispatched to investigate. Initially, he wasn’t a Bigfoot believer. One account says he suspected that people possibly moonshiners might be responsible for harassing the couple.

2. The really creepy part

The couple eventually told Akin that they believed the creature was imitating or responding to them. One particularly memorable part of the story involves the couple’s dog. According to later accounts of Akin’s story, the creature appeared to imitate the way the owners called their dog, apparently attempting to lure it outside.

There were also reports of something walking alongside the exterior of the trailer and making noises at the occupants. The turning point came when the property owner took Deputy Akin down toward Elkins Creek. There were reportedly five enormous footprints along the creek bank. Four were largely submerged in the creek, but one remained in soft silt and was sufficiently preserved to make a cast.

Akin made a plaster impression of the footprint. The resulting cast measured approximately:

17.5 inches long × 8.5 inches wide.

That’s the object that eventually became known as the Elkins Creek Cast.
